title: x-consequence (RFC 0001, draft)
description: Consequence contract: what an action does to the world, and the confirmation, recovery and authentication that class of action requires. Normative text: rfcs/0001-temporal-and-consequence.md.

prop.description: For a generic action component: the prop with which each usage declares its consequence class. The prop must be a union whose values are consequence classes.

policies.description: For a generic action component: the treatment each class requires around this component. Keys are consequence classes.

actions.description: For a component that owns its actions: each action, its class and the treatment it actually gets, as a verifiable claim.

class.description: reversible: the user can undo it. irreversible: destroys data or state with no recovery. external: sends something to another person or system and cannot be recalled. financial: commits or moves money. privacy: discloses personal data beyond the user's own view. identity: changes credentials, ownership or authentication factors.

confirmation.description: Ordered weakest to strongest. review: the user sees exactly what will happen or be sent before committing. explicit: a separate confirming action names the consequence. typed: the user types a confirming value.

recovery.description: undo: a time-boxed undo restores the prior state. inverse-action: a separate action reverses it at any time.

authentication.description: Ordered weakest to strongest. recent: a sign-in within a short window. step-up: re-authenticate for this action.

tone.description: The tone value the triggering control must use, e.g. error for irreversible.

rule.description: Id of a usage rule (section 4 of the spec) that enforces part of this policy statically.
